questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Netherlands?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Netherlands article.

questions.proof: The official capital of the Netherlands is Amsterdam.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Netherlands?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Netherlands article.

questions.proof: The language of the Netherlands is also called Dutch.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “To the north and west of the European part of the Netherlands is the North Sea, and to the east is _____, and to the south is Belgium.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “east”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Netherlands article.

questions.proof: To the north and west of the European part of the Netherlands is the North Sea, and to the east is Germany, and to the south is Belgium.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “According to a survey done in _____, 23% of the Dutch people are Christian and 6% is islam and 71% believe in another organised religion, like Judaism, Islam or Hinduism.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twenty-first century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “People” part of the Netherlands article.

questions.proof: According to a survey done in 2010, 23% of the Dutch people are Christian and 6% is islam and 71% believe in another organised religion, like Judaism, Islam or Hinduism.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “In 1831 the Belgians chose their own king and _____ became an independent country.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “became”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Netherlands article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: In 1831 the Belgians chose their own king and Belgium became an independent country.
